subject: Biology
title: Honeybees and pollen
intro: Honeybees live in large colonies and spend much of the warm season collecting food from flowers.

facts.text: A worker bee visits dozens of flowers on a single trip, and pollen sticks to the tiny hairs on her body.
facts.ev: Pollen sticks to the tiny hairs on a worker bee's body as she visits dozens of flowers on one trip.

facts.text: When a bee lands on the next flower, some of that pollen rubs off onto the part of the flower that makes seeds.
facts.ev: Some pollen rubs off onto the seed-making part of the next flower a bee lands on.
facts.tag: pollen rubbing off on the next flower

facts.text: Many fruits and vegetables, including apples and squash, only form when pollen reaches their flowers.
facts.ev: The source points out that foods such as apples and squash only form after pollen reaches their flowers.

facts.text: A single hive can hold more than 20,000 bees, and thousands of them search for food each day.
facts.ev: A single hive can hold more than 20,000 bees, with thousands searching for food every day.

facts.text: Bees drink nectar, a sugary liquid inside flowers, and use it to make honey.
facts.ev: Bees drink nectar from flowers and use it to make honey.

facts.text: Honeybees communicate by dancing, and the pattern of a dance tells other bees where flowers are located.
facts.ev: The pattern of a honeybee's dance tells hive mates where flowers are located.

facts.text: In winter, honeybees cluster together inside the hive and eat stored honey to stay warm.
facts.ev: In winter, honeybees cluster inside the hive and eat stored honey to stay warm.

facts.text: A honeybee's wings beat about 200 times per second, which produces the buzzing sound people hear.
facts.ev: A honeybee's wings beat about 200 times per second, producing the buzzing sound people hear.

models.q: How do honeybees help flowering plants reproduce?
models.restate: Honeybees help flowering plants reproduce in an important way.
models.answer: Honeybees carry pollen from flower to flower, which allows plants to make seeds.
exp: Because the hairs hold the pollen, the bee is carrying plant material from one flower toward the next.
Pollen that reaches the seed-making part of a flower can start the process of forming seeds.
rep: A bee's body hairs hold pollen as she travels among dozens of flowers.
Pollen rubs off onto flowers when a bee lands on them.
models.sum: In short, honeybees move pollen between flowers, and that movement lets plants make seeds.
models.sumNew: In short, honeybees move pollen between flowers, and they also huddle in the hive during winter to eat stored honey.
models.bad: Honeybees help plants reproduce by planting seeds in the soil beneath each flower.
models.badRestate: Honeybees spend the warm season gathering food for their colonies.
models.offExp: Because nectar is sugary, bees can turn it into honey that feeds the colony.

models.q: Why are honeybees important for the food people eat?
models.restate: Honeybees play a part in providing the food that people eat.
models.answer: Honeybees matter for food supplies because many crops depend on the pollen they spread.
exp: Since these foods depend on pollen, the bees that deliver it help make the harvest possible.
With so many bees working each day, pollen can be spread across a very large number of flowers.
rep: Apples and squash form only when pollen reaches their flowers.
A hive holds more than 20,000 bees, and thousands search for food daily.
models.sum: The pollen-spreading work of honeybees supports the production of foods that people rely on.
models.sumNew: The pollen-spreading work of honeybees supports our food, and their wings beat about 200 times per second.
models.bad: Honeybees matter for food because they grow apples and squash inside their hives.
models.badRestate: Honeybees make a buzzing sound that people hear whenever the bees fly.
models.offExp: Because the wings beat so quickly, the air vibrates and people hear a steady buzz.

subject: Energy and technology
title: Solar panels
intro: Solar panels are flat devices made of many small cells that capture energy from sunlight.

facts.text: Each cell in a solar panel is made of a material that produces an electric current when light strikes it.
facts.ev: A solar cell produces an electric current whenever light strikes its surface.

facts.text: Panels have no moving parts, so they make electricity quietly and need little repair.
facts.ev: Panels have no moving parts, so they work quietly and need little repair.

facts.text: Panels can be bolted onto rooftops, which lets a building use space that is otherwise empty.
facts.ev: Panels can be bolted onto rooftops, using space that is otherwise empty.

facts.text: On cloudy days, a panel still produces some electricity, though usually less than on a bright day.
facts.ev: The passage notes that even on cloudy days a panel produces some electricity, though less than in bright sunlight.

facts.text: A solar panel does not burn fuel while it operates, so it gives off no smoke.
facts.ev: An operating panel burns no fuel and gives off no smoke.

facts.text: Some calculators contain tiny solar cells that let them run without batteries.
facts.ev: Certain calculators run on tiny solar cells instead of batteries.

facts.text: Engineers measure a panel's output in watts, which describes how much power it can produce.
facts.ev: Engineers describe how much power a panel can produce by measuring its output in watts.

facts.text: The first practical silicon solar cell was announced in 1954.
facts.ev: The first practical silicon solar cell was announced in 1954.

models.q: What makes solar panels a practical way to make electricity?
models.restate: Solar panels are a practical way to make electricity because of how they work and where they can go.
models.answer: Solar panels are practical because they turn light directly into electricity and fit onto spaces that already exist.
exp: That means sunlight itself becomes the source of power, with no extra step such as burning something.
Using a roof lets a building produce power without needing a new piece of land.
rep: Light that strikes a cell causes it to produce an electric current.
Panels are placed on rooftops that would otherwise be empty.
models.sum: Altogether, panels are practical because they change light into electricity and can sit on spaces buildings already have.
models.sumNew: Altogether, panels are practical because they change light into electricity, and engineers rate each one in watts.
models.bad: Solar panels are practical because they store enough energy to power a building for a year without sunlight.
models.badRestate: Panels come in many sizes and are rated by how much power they can produce.
models.offExp: Because output is measured in watts, buyers can compare how much power different panels produce.

models.q: Is a solar panel a dependable source of electricity?
models.restate: Whether a solar panel is dependable depends on how it is built and how it performs in different weather.
models.answer: Solar panels are fairly dependable because they have few parts that can wear out and still work in weak light.
exp: With nothing mechanical to break down, a panel is less likely to stop working than a machine with many moving pieces.
Producing at least some power under clouds means electricity does not disappear whenever the sky is not clear.
rep: Panels contain no moving parts and work quietly with little repair.
A cloudy day still produces some electricity, but less than a bright day.
models.sum: The simple design and partial cloudy-day output together make solar panels a reasonably dependable source of electricity.
models.sumNew: The simple design and partial cloudy-day output make panels dependable, and they also burn no fuel or give off smoke.
models.bad: Solar panels are dependable because they make exactly the same amount of electricity every hour of the day.
models.badRestate: Solar panels are helpful because they do not burn fuel or give off smoke while operating.
models.offExp: Since no fuel is burned, the panel itself does not release smoke into the air around it.

subject: Earth science
title: The water cycle
intro: Water on Earth is always moving between the oceans, the air, and the land in a pattern called the water cycle.

facts.text: The Sun warms the surface of oceans and lakes, and some liquid water changes into an invisible gas called water vapor.
facts.ev: Heat from the Sun turns some water from oceans and lakes into an invisible gas called water vapor.

facts.text: As water vapor rises, the air around it cools, and the vapor changes back into tiny droplets that form clouds.
facts.ev: Rising water vapor cools and changes back into tiny droplets that form clouds.

facts.text: When droplets in a cloud join together and grow heavy, they fall to the ground as rain, snow, or hail.
facts.ev: Cloud droplets that join together and grow heavy fall as rain, snow, or hail.

facts.text: Rain that lands on hills and mountains flows downhill into streams and rivers, which carry the water toward the sea.
facts.ev: As the source describes, rain on hills and mountains flows downhill into streams and rivers that carry the water toward the sea.

facts.text: Plants take in water through their roots and release some of it as vapor through tiny openings in their leaves.
facts.ev: Plants take in water through their roots and release part of it as vapor through their leaves.

facts.text: About 97 percent of Earth's water is salt water found in the oceans.
facts.ev: About 97 percent of Earth's water is salt water found in the oceans.

facts.text: Some rain soaks into the soil and becomes groundwater, which can stay underground for many years.
facts.ev: Some rain soaks into the soil and becomes groundwater that can stay underground for many years.

facts.text: Fog forms when water vapor cools into droplets close to the ground instead of high in the sky.
facts.ev: Fog forms when water vapor cools into droplets close to the ground.

models.q: How does ocean water end up as clouds and rain?
models.restate: Water from the ocean can become clouds and rain through a series of steps.
models.answer: Heat lifts ocean water into the air as vapor, and cooling turns that vapor into the clouds that produce rain.
exp: Without this first step, liquid water would stay in the ocean and never enter the air.
Clouds are where the scattered vapor gathers again as droplets, linking the water in the air to the rain that falls.
rep: The Sun's heat changes some of the water from oceans and lakes into water vapor.
Vapor that rises into cooler air changes into tiny droplets that make up clouds.
models.sum: In short, the Sun's heat lifts water into the air, and cooling turns it into the clouds that bring rain.
models.sumNew: In short, the Sun's heat lifts water into the air and cooling forms clouds, and about 97 percent of Earth's water is salty ocean water.
models.bad: Ocean water becomes rain when the wind pushes the waves up into the sky until they freeze.
models.badRestate: Most of the water on Earth is found in the oceans.
models.offExp: Because so much of Earth's water is in the oceans, most of the planet's water is salty.

models.q: Why does water on Earth keep moving instead of staying in one place?
models.restate: Earth's water keeps moving from place to place rather than staying in one spot.
models.answer: Water keeps moving because the Sun's heat lifts it into the air and falling rain carries it back toward the sea.
exp: Since the Sun keeps warming oceans and lakes, water is repeatedly lifted out of them as vapor.
Because the water flows downhill, rain that falls on high ground is carried back toward the sea, which completes the loop.
rep: The Sun warms oceans and lakes, and some of the water becomes invisible vapor.
Rain that lands on mountains flows downhill into streams and rivers.
models.sum: Water is always on the move because the Sun lifts it into the air and flowing rain returns it.
models.sumNew: Water is always on the move because the Sun lifts it into the air and flowing rain returns it, and some even soaks into the ground for many years.
models.bad: Water keeps moving because the ocean is pulled from one side of the planet to the other by the Moon.
models.badRestate: Some rain sinks into the ground instead of flowing to streams and rivers.
models.offExp: Because groundwater can stay underground for years, some of the water leaves the visible cycle for a long time.

subject: Engineering and architecture
title: Arch bridges
intro: An arch bridge uses a curved shape to carry the weight of the roadway and everything that travels across it.

facts.text: The curve of an arch pushes weight outward and downward along the curve, toward the supports at each end.
facts.ev: The curve of an arch pushes weight outward and downward toward the supports at each end.

facts.text: Stone arches built by Roman engineers about two thousand years ago still stand in parts of Europe.
facts.ev: Stone arches built by Roman engineers about two thousand years ago still stand in parts of Europe.

facts.text: Because stone resists squeezing very well, a stone arch stays strong as long as its pieces are pressed tightly together.
facts.ev: A stone arch stays strong as long as its pieces are pressed tightly together, since stone resists squeezing very well.

facts.text: The supports at the ends of an arch, called abutments, must be firmly anchored in the ground or in solid rock.
facts.ev: The supports at the ends of an arch, called abutments, must be firmly anchored in the ground or in solid rock.

facts.text: Arch bridges can span wide gaps, such as rivers and valleys, without placing many supports in the water.
facts.ev: According to the text, arch bridges can span rivers and valleys without placing many supports in the water.

facts.text: Modern arches are often built from steel or concrete, which can be shaped into long, thin curves.
facts.ev: Modern arches are often built from steel or concrete, which can be shaped into long, thin curves.

facts.text: A bridge builder first constructs a temporary wooden frame, which holds the stones in place until the arch is complete.
facts.ev: Builders first make a temporary wooden frame that holds the stones in place until the arch is complete.

facts.text: Many arch bridges have a smooth, curved outline that people consider attractive.
facts.ev: Many arch bridges have a smooth, curved outline that people consider attractive.

models.q: Why is an arch a strong shape for a bridge?
models.restate: The arch shape gives a bridge a great deal of strength.
models.answer: An arch is strong because its curve directs the weight of the bridge toward solid supports.
exp: Sending the load along the curve means that no single spot has to hold up all of the weight alone.
Pressing the stones together uses the very kind of force that stone handles best.
rep: The curve of an arch pushes weight outward and downward toward the end supports.
A stone arch remains strong as long as its pieces are pressed together tightly.
models.sum: An arch stays strong because its curve guides weight to the supports and keeps the stone pieces pressed together.
models.sumNew: An arch stays strong because its curve guides weight to the supports, and its smooth outline is considered attractive.
models.bad: An arch is strong because the roadway on top of it is made from the hardest stone in the world.
models.badRestate: The look of an arch bridge is one reason people enjoy these structures.
models.offExp: Since people find the smooth outline pleasing, an arch can make a bridge look graceful.

models.q: What advantages do arch bridges offer for crossing rivers and valleys?
models.restate: Arch bridges offer certain advantages when builders need to cross rivers and valleys.
models.answer: Arch bridges suit wide crossings because they can stretch across gaps and can last for centuries.
exp: Needing fewer supports in the water means builders face fewer difficulties working in the river itself.
Structures that still stand after about two thousand years show how durable a well-built arch can be.
rep: Arch bridges can cross rivers and valleys without many supports in the water.
Roman stone arches from about two thousand years ago still stand in parts of Europe.
models.sum: Overall, arches suit rivers and valleys because they cross wide gaps and can remain in use for a very long time.
models.sumNew: Overall, arches suit rivers and valleys because they cross wide gaps and last, and builders use a temporary wooden frame while constructing them.
models.bad: Arch bridges are the best choice for crossing any gap because they never need any repairs.
models.badRestate: Builders construct a temporary frame to hold the stones while an arch is built.
models.offExp: Because the frame supports the stones during construction, builders can place each piece safely before the arch is finished.

subject: Libraries and education
title: Public libraries
intro: A public library is a community resource that lends books and other materials to people who live nearby.

facts.text: With a library card, a person can borrow books for a few weeks at no charge and return them when finished.
facts.ev: With a library card, a person can borrow books for a few weeks at no charge.

facts.text: Many libraries offer computers and internet access, which people can use for homework and job applications.
facts.ev: Many libraries provide computers and internet access that people can use for homework and job applications.

facts.text: Libraries host free programs, such as reading hours for young children and tutoring for students.
facts.ev: The passage says libraries host free programs, including reading hours for young children and tutoring for students.

facts.text: Librarians help visitors find reliable sources and teach them how to search for information.
facts.ev: Librarians help visitors find reliable sources and teach them how to search for information.

facts.text: Some libraries stay open late in the evening so that people who work during the day can visit.

facts.text: Libraries buy books in large numbers and share each copy with many different readers.

models.q: How do public libraries help students learn?
models.restate: Public libraries support students' learning in several ways.
models.answer: Libraries help students learn by giving them free access to reading materials and to tools for schoolwork.
exp: Since the books cost nothing to borrow, students can read widely without spending any money.
A student who has no computer at home can still finish assignments that require one.
rep: A person with a library card can borrow books at no charge for a few weeks.
Libraries provide computers and internet access for homework and job applications.
models.sum: Libraries help students learn by offering free books and the technology needed for assignments.
models.sumNew: Libraries help students learn by offering free books and technology, and the oldest known libraries held clay tablets.
models.bad: Libraries help students learn by writing each student's homework assignments for them.

models.q: Why is a library a valuable resource for a whole community?
models.restate: A library serves an entire community, not only people who already read often.
models.answer: A library is valuable to a whole community because it offers programs and expert help that people of many ages can use.
exp: Reading hours for young children and tutoring for students show that the library serves different age groups.
Guidance in finding reliable sources helps visitors judge information, a skill useful at any age.
rep: Libraries host free programs, including reading hours and tutoring.
Librarians help visitors locate reliable sources and show them how to search.
models.sum: By offering programs and guidance, a library benefits people of every age in the whole community.
models.sumNew: By offering programs and guidance, a library benefits the whole community, and its buildings often have quiet rooms for studying.
models.bad: A library is valuable to a community because it pays visitors to read books every day.
models.badRestate: Many library buildings include quiet rooms where visitors can study.
models.offExp: Because the rooms are quiet, students can concentrate while they study.
